senses.gloss: (preced.) [to squeeze in, make a hole,]

units: <cite ref="Bava Batra 7b:13">B. Bath. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>קְבַע וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="M01969"><he>מַסְמָר</he></cite>. Tanḥ. B’haʿal. 15 (ref. to <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 12:11">Koh. XII, 11</cite> <he>משמרות</he>) <he>אם קָבַעְתָּ אותם כמ̇ס̇מ̇ר̇ בלבך הן מ̇ש̇מ̇ר̇ין אותך</he> if thou hast driven them (the words of the Law) like a nail into thy heart, they will guard thee.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 5:5">Lev. R. s. 5</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 22:16">Is. XXII, 16</cite>) <he>אפי׳ איזה מסמר קבעת כאן</he> what nail hast thou driven into it (to acquire ownership)? <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 10:6">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. X, 6</cite> <he>אע״פ שקְבָעָן וכ׳</he> (not <he>שקבאן</he>) although he fastened them with nails; a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>קָבוּעַ</he>; f. <he>קְבוּעָה</he> &c.

Ib. צריך אדם … יתד ק׳ וכ׳ a man ought to have a nail or a peg fixed in the burial ground so as to take possession and be sure to be buried in the designated place. Y. Maas. Sh. V, beg. 55ᵈ אבן ק׳ a stone affixed to the ground, stationary, opp. תלושה; a. fr.—Trnsf. to fix, appoint, make permanent.
<cite ref="Berakhot 6b:6">Ber. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>כל הקוֹבֵעַ מקום וכ׳</he> he who designates a certain place where to pray regularly; <cite ref="Berakhot 7b">ib. 7ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Megillah 7a:2">Meg. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>בתחלה קְבָעוּהָ וכ׳</he> at first they instituted the feast of Purim for Shushan, and afterwards for the whole world.
<cite ref="Megillah 7a:3">Ib.</cite> <he>שלחה … קִבְעוּנִי לדורות</he> Esther sent word to the scholars, Appoint my memory to be celebrated for all generations.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:2">Ab. III, 2</cite> <he>הקב״ה קובע לו שכר</he> the Lord will determine his reward.

<cite ref="Beitzah 20a:13">Bets. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>בקשו לִקְבּוֹעַ הלכה וכ׳</he> they attempted (by vote) to establish the law in agreement with their opinion; <cite ref="Tosefta Chagigah 2:11">Tosef. Ḥag. II, 11</cite>; a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab.
<cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 1:1">Tosef. Ab. Zar. I, 1</cite> <he>אידין הקְבוּעִין</he> regular (annual) festivals.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 11b:8">Ab. Zar. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>חמשה בתי ע״ז ק׳ הן</he> five idolatrous temples (and the fairs connected therewith) are permanent; expl.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 11b:9">ib.</cite> <he>לעולם תדירא וכ׳</he> permanent, regular, and all the year through &c. B. Bath. l. c. <he>הלכות קְבוּעוֹת הן</he> they are established laws; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (denom. of קֶבַע) to impart the character of a regular appointed meal.
units: <cite ref="Beitzah 34b:3">Bets. 34ᵇ</cite> <he>שבת מהו שתִּקְבַּע מוקצה למעשר</he> does the Sabbath give, to fruit not yet ready for regular use, the character of an appointed meal with reference to the duty of tithing (so that you dare not eat of them on the Sabbath even as a luncheon, <he>אכילת עראי</he>)? <cite ref="Beitzah 34b:3">Ib.</cite> <he>שבת קוֹבַעַת וכ׳</he> the Sabbath gives that character, whether the food you partake of be sufficiently ready for consumption or not.

<cite ref="Pesachim 105a:3">Pes. 105ᵃ</cite> <he>כשם שהשבת … קובעת לקידוש</he> as the Sabbath makes every meal an appointed one with regard to tithes, so does it with reference to Ḳiddush (that you dare not taste anything before reciting the Ḳiddush, v. <cite ref="S00873"><he>קִידּוּשׁ</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Pesachim 105a:3">Ib.</cite> <he>קָבְעָה להבדלה</he> the exit of the Sabbath makes every meal an appointed one as regards the Habdalah (v. <cite ref="E00028"><he>הַבְדָּלָה</he></cite>); a. fr.

<cite ref="Shabbat 67b">Sabb. 67ᵇ</cite> <he>המְקַבַּעַת</he> Rashi Var., v. <cite ref="B01128"><he>בָּקַע</he></cite>.—Part. pass. <cite ref="M02570"><he>מְקוּבַּע</he></cite>; f. <he>מְקוּבַּעַת</he>.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12">Num. R. s. 12</cite> <he>כעטרה הזאת שמק׳ באבנים וכ׳</he> like the royal crown which is beset with precious stones and pearls.

<cite ref="Tosefta Chagigah 2:11">Tosef. Ḥag. II, 11</cite> <he>נִקְבְּעָה הלכה כדברי וכ׳</he> the law was established (by vote) in accordance with the opinion of &c.; (<cite ref="Beitzah 20b:1">Bets. 20ᵇ</cite> <he>וקבעו וכ׳</he>). Y. Yoma V, beg. 42ᵇ <he>שאין … נִקְבָּעִין אלא וכ׳</he> congregational sacrifices are designated as such only by the act of slaughtering.
<cite ref="Mishnah Challah 4:11">Ḥall. IV, 11</cite> <he>שלא יִקָּבַע הרבר חובה</he> that this usage may not become an established obligation; a. e.
